newsitem.title: UK: P&O ferry passengers fall in year.
newsitem.headline: P&O ferry passengers fall in year.

text.p: Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co said on Thursday that total ferry passengers in 1996 fell to 11.1 million from 12.2 million in 1995.
However, the ferry operator said that as a result of the Channel Tunnel fire European ferry passengers increased to 2.3 million from 2.0 million in the fourth quarter of 1995.

P&O said in a statement that numbers of passengers and tourist vehicles and freight all increased in the fourth quarter as a whole by 15 percent on the busy short-sea crossing between Dover in southern England and Calais in France.

Tough competition from the Channel Tunnel run by Eurotunnel led to P&O and Swedish ferry operator Stena Line AB announcing a merger of their businesses on the cross-channel ferry market last year under a new joint venture.
However, the British government's Monoplies and Mergers Commission (MMC) is still investigating the merger.
The latest quarterly P&O figures also reported tough times for containers, which saw revenues for the fourth quarter fall back, reflecting poor Far East to Europe trade.

"The strengthening of sterling against other currencies in the final quarter has had an adverse affect, although for the year as a whole this position has not been as marked as in 1995," the company said in a statement.
The cruises unit was reported to have had a steady year with cruise 1996 load factor at 99.7 percent versus 99.9 percent, but P&O noted that fourth quarter yields were down slightly.
P&O said that advance bookings and yields for 1997 are ahead of those at the same time last year.
In the year, P&O's Princess and P&O cruise units achieved total capacity of 5.4 million versus 4.7 million in 1995.
